correctness.rationale: The sample map is invertible since the nodes are distinct on a proper arc. Independently prescribing the two complex sample phases attains the sum of Lagrange coefficient moduli at a fixed evaluation point. With x=(v-u)/4 and m=(u+v)/2, this quotient is cos((t-m)/2)/cos x between the nodes and |sin((t-m)/2)|/sin x outside. On the longer exterior interval the distance from m runs from 2x to theta+|m|, and 2x<pi, so the maximum is at the far endpoint or at distance pi, giving exactly the capped-sine expression. This also handles arcs longer than a semicircle and the degenerate exterior intervals at endpoint nodes. Balancing sec x and sin(theta/2)/sin x proves the unique optimal separation; the cap is strictly above sin(theta/2) for m≠0, so only the centered pair attains the bound. The endpoint norm and the monotonicity and limits of C_theta follow directly. Independent chord-sum grid comparisons at four apertures, including asymmetric and capped cases, were consistent (python /workspace/review_checks.py, check 5); the analytic argument, not the grid, verifies the continuum statement.
